title: Acme Foods: the next data platform
subtitle: Which platform the brief of 19 October 2026 calls for, and which options it rules out.

verdict.text: Build a lakehouse in layers with one streaming path, used only by the shelf-sensor stock feed, while the other 13 sources load daily. The binding constraint is who can run it: one central team of six, with no business unit that has its own engineers, rules out a data mesh, the only option above this one.

Retention, budget and cloud vendor. Also whether sources must be joined, keep history or can take the reporting load. Those last three stay unset in the rules, because they only bear on reports on the source, which photos and model training already rule out. [high]

sections.title: Assumptions
sections.intro: You asked me not to stop for questions, so each gap is filled here, next to the decision it drives.

items: The 2 minutes run end to end, from the sensor reading to the ordering team's screen, and the team really acts inside that window [med]. **Drives:** the streaming path. At 5 minutes or more a scheduled load is enough and the path goes.

Personal data is not only in the CRM. The current repo has customer name, email, phone, national ID and birth date in the ERP (`models/staging/stg_customers.sql`) [high]. The HR roster, loyalty app, delivery files, web events, tills and returns desk probably hold some too [med]. **Drives:** one masking gate for every table source, not a rule for the CRM alone.
Shelf camera photos can show shoppers or staff [guess]. **Drives:** photos get their own restricted raw store, and the reach view below counts them as personal data.
EU-only covers storage, backups, processing, logs and the control planes of managed services, not only the main storage [med]. **Drives:** the residency acceptance test and the vendor shortlist.

Object storage, compute and the event log are managed services in an EU region, not self-hosted [guess; no vendor checked]. **Drives:** the team rating. Six engineers can carry one managed streaming path, and a self-hosted broker on top of 14 sources would be a different answer.
35 TB covers all 14 sources and grows in a straight line with nothing deleted [med]. **Drives:** the sizing only. Files, model training and the 2-minute feed rule out the smaller options at any size.
Retention in the Layers table is a proposal, because the brief sets none [guess]. **Drives:** storage volume and how far an erasure request has to reach.
Budget is not in the brief, so cost is compared only relatively [high]. **Drives:** the Cost column, which decides nothing here.

The marketing mailing in the current repo (`exports/marketing_contacts.sql`) stays out of scope, because the brief does not name it [med]. **Drives:** no contact export is drawn, and nothing leaves Cleaned except through the masking gate.

blocks.text:
**The binding constraint is who can run it.** The next option up, a data mesh, needs at least three domain teams with their own engineers. Acme has none and plans none (`too-few-domains`), so one central team of six means one shared platform owned in one place.

**One feed and one model set the floor.** Original photos for training rule out everything below a lakehouse (`needs-file-storage`, `ml-on-raw`). The 2-minute stock feed then rules out a lakehouse without a streaming path (`needs-streaming`). Size matters less than it looks: the 59 TB rules out only the single database.

**A warehouse with a bucket on the side is not a cheaper way out.** It would still need a store for the photos and a streaming path for the feed, and it would add a second access model for the same six people to govern [med].

**The streaming path stays narrow on purpose.** It carries one feed, from 12 stores according to the repo README [med], so the load is small. The real cost is that it must run whenever the stores are open, and that is why the team rating is weak and not a pass.

sections.title: What would change it
sections.intro: Each option named here comes from running the rules again with the changed fact.

items: **The ordering team can work with 5 minutes or more:** a lakehouse in layers, with no streaming path. This is the cheapest thing to confirm, so ask them first.
**Volume ×10 (590 TB after two years):** the same option. The rules do not move, and the work shifts to storage tiering for photos and compaction.
**A use that needs seconds, or more feeds under 5 minutes:** the same option with a wider streaming path. Past about three feeds it needs its own named owner [guess].
**Three or more business units hire their own engineers:** a data mesh becomes open, and the central team would become its platform team.
**Photos and PDFs leave scope, the model is dropped and the feed relaxes to 5 minutes:** a managed warehouse, provided sources must be joined, which the brief implies but does not state.

blocks.code:
# ADR-001: A lakehouse in layers with one streaming path for the shelf stock feed

Date: 2026-11-09
Status: Proposed

## Context
Acme Foods' reporting grew by hand around the store sales figures and no longer covers
what the business asks for (brief, 19 October 2026). There are 14 sources, 35 TB today,
growing about 1 TB a month, so 59 TB after two years. One stock feed from the shelf
sensors must be under 2 minutes fresh so the ordering team can act on an empty shelf.
Every other source is daily. Data scientists train a shelf-image model on original
photos from the store cameras. All data must stay in the EU, including backups. The
CRM holds personal data of loyalty customers. Six data engineers in one central team
build and run everything, business units have no engineers of their own, and 120 BI
users read the reports.

## Decision
We will build one lakehouse in raw, cleaned and served layers, in EU regions only,
including backups, run by the central team.
We will load every source daily except the shelf-sensor stock feed, which takes a
streaming path ending in a live stock view for the ordering team. That feed is also
archived to raw.
We will keep original photos in a separate restricted raw store, read only by a named
data science group.
We will mask or drop personal data at one point, between cleaned and served.
We will not build a data mesh, because no business unit has its own engineers.

## Consequences
Easier: tables, files and photos live under one access model, any load can be
replayed from raw, and new daily sources need no new infrastructure.
Harder: six engineers carry an always-on path for one feed, which must be watched
whenever the stores are open. Live stock and daily stock must be reconciled.
We accept that data scientists read original photos unmasked, inside a restricted
store, until the data protection owner rules on whether the photos show people. We
accept that the streaming path is cost for one feed, and it goes if the ordering team
can work with 5 minutes or more.

items: **Do the shelf cameras capture shoppers or staff?** If they do, the raw photo route needs a data protection impact assessment and a decision on blurring before the first training run.

**What does EU-only mean for people and stores outside the EU?** The repo README places Acme in Novi Sad, which is outside the EU [high]. The brief does not say whether the rule also covers store systems there, or engineers reading the data from there. Legal should answer this before a vendor is picked.

**Does the marketing mailing move to the new platform?** Today `exports/marketing_contacts.sql` hands names, email and national ID to a campaign tool by hand [high]. The brief does not mention it. If it moves, it needs its own consent-checked route, without the national ID.
**How fast does the ordering team really act, and during which hours?** This confirms the 2 minutes and sets the on-call hours for the streaming path.
**What retention applies to each source, and what is the budget?** Neither is in the brief. Prices should come from a costing pass once a vendor and EU region are named.
**How much of the 35 TB is photos?** It changes storage tiering and the cost of the raw layer, not the decision.
**What happens to the current warehouse?** The dbt models, the T-SQL procedures and the Spark stock notebook need a migration plan, and the brief does not cover one.
